titel: Designer Outlet Roermond: a day trip from Hotel Asteria Venray
omschrijving: Designer Outlet Roermond is a 40-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray. How to avoid the crowds and end the day with wellness and dinner.
hero-sub: Around 170 shops on the edge of Roermond's town centre, a 40-minute drive from Hotel Asteria in Venray.
hero-alt: Entrance to Designer Outlet Roermond in a brick building with two clocks
oog-kop: Designer Outlet Roermond at a glance
v1-kop: A day of shopping in Roermond
v1-p1: Designer Outlet Roermond is an open-air shopping centre with around 170 designer brand stores selling their collections at reduced prices. From Hotel Asteria it is a drive of about 40 minutes, just under 50 kilometres. So it is not an outing round the corner, but a full day out.
v1-p2: You stroll along little streets lined with shops, with places for a coffee or a quick bite in between, such as Starbucks and Frankie's with churros. The centre is mostly on one level, with ramps and lifts to the higher parts. You can drop your purchases in a locker along the way, which you book and pay for on your phone.
v1-alt: The tower of St Christopher's Cathedral above the shops of Designer Outlet Roermond
v1-knop: Shops and opening hours on mcarthurglen.com
v2-p1: The outlet draws many visitors from Germany. On German public holidays, when the shops across the border are closed, it gets especially busy. In Roermond, Good Friday is even known as 'German Day', and the municipality then diverts traffic to limit queues at the outlet. So when you plan, check the German public holidays, as well as event days such as the Black Friday Days at the end of November.
v2-p2: You park in the outlet's car parks and garages. The first half hour is free and a whole day costs €7. Premium Parking by the main entrance costs €12.50 a day. Disabled parking spaces are on P1, and charging points on P1, P2 and at Premium Parking.
v2-alt: Shopping street with half-timbered facades in Designer Outlet Roermond
v3-kop: Combine it with the town centre
v3-p1: Roermond's historic town centre is a few minutes' walk from the outlet. On the Markt stands St Christopher's Cathedral, and a little further on the Munsterkerk, a Romanesque church from the 13th century. If you would rather have lunch on a terrace in town than among the shops, simply leave the car where it is.
v3-alt: The Markt in Roermond with St Christopher's Cathedral
tip: Go on a weekday rather than a Saturday and leave straight after breakfast, so you arrive around opening time. Avoid German public holidays. And book a table in our brasserie before you set off, so after the sauna you have nothing left to think about.
g1-tekst: Sundays too. Current opening hours, including around public holidays, are on mcarthurglen.com.
g1-alt: Entrance to Designer Outlet Roermond with flags and autumn trees
g2-tekst: First 30 minutes free, then €7 a day. Charging points on P1, P2 and at Premium Parking.
g2-alt: Aerial view of Designer Outlet Roermond with the car parks by the water
g3-tekst: On a lead. Some shops and restaurants do not allow dogs.
g3-alt: White facade with blue awnings in Designer Outlet Roermond
g4-tekst: Free to borrow from Guest Services against a deposit. The centre is mostly on one level.
g4-alt: Entrance to Designer Outlet Roermond with the Ferris wheel at Christmas
dag-sub: Breakfast at the hotel, shopping in Roermond during the day and back in the late afternoon for the sauna and dinner.
m1-tekst: The breakfast buffet is served from 07.00 to 10.00 on weekdays and from 08.00 to 10.30 at weekends. Leave at half past nine and on a weekday you will be in Roermond around opening time.
m1-alt: Breakfast buffet in the restaurant of Hotel Asteria
m2-tekst: Take your time in the shops and have lunch at the outlet or in the town centre, a few minutes' walk away. You can drop your purchases in a locker along the way.
m2-alt: Designer Outlet sign next to the tower of St Christopher's Cathedral
m3-tekst: After the 40-minute drive, you warm up in the sauna. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 16.00 to 22.00 and Friday to Sunday from 12.00 to 22.00. Tuesday is swimwear day.
m3-alt: Foot bath in the wellness area on the Top Floor
m4-tekst: You end the day at a table in the hotel's brasserie. The kitchen is open until 21.30, and afterwards your room is just a lift ride away.
m4-alt: Bar in the brasserie of Hotel Asteria
kamers-sub: After a day of shopping and an evening in the sauna, you would rather not drive home. Choose your room; you will see the price for your dates straight away when you book.
kaart-regel: Designer Outlet Roermond lies south of Venray, on the edge of Roermond's town centre. The map also shows three outings closer to the hotel.
kaart-naam: Designer Outlet Roermond, Stadsweide 2, 6041 TD Roermond
kaart-alt: Map of North and Central Limburg with Hotel Asteria in Venray, Designer Outlet Roermond and three other outings
f1-v: How far is Designer Outlet Roermond from Hotel Asteria?
f1-a: It is 49.3 kilometres, about 40 minutes by car. On German public holidays and event days the roads around Roermond can be busy, so allow extra time. Parking at Hotel Asteria is free.
f2-v: How much time should I allow?
f2-a: Allow a day. With around 170 shops and the town centre within walking distance, a few hours go by quickly, and the drive there and back takes about an hour and a half in total. The outlet is open every day; in November 2026 from 10.00 to 20.00 on weekdays and from 09.00 to 21.00 at weekends. On the Black Friday Days, 20 to 22 and 27 to 29 November, it stays open until 22.00.
f3-v: Is the outlet a good outing on a rainy day?
f3-a: The outlet is an open-air shopping centre: you walk outside between the shops. So bring an umbrella in bad weather. Inside the shops and at the coffee spots you stay dry.
f4-v: Do I need to buy tickets or book anything in advance?
f4-a: No, entry is free. Only parking costs money: the first half hour is free, a whole day €7 and Premium Parking by the main entrance €12.50 (November 2026). You can reserve a wheelchair online in advance; you borrow it free of charge against a €50 deposit.
f5-v: Can I bring my dog to the outlet?
f5-a: Yes, on a lead. Some shops and restaurants may refuse dogs. There is a drinking fountain for dogs at Timberland, and you can pick up free poo bags at Guest Services.
f6-v: Can I still use the wellness area and have dinner at the hotel after shopping?
f6-a: Yes. The wellness area is open Monday to Thursday from 16.00 to 22.00 and Friday to Sunday from 12.00 to 22.00. Tuesday is swimwear day. You can have dinner in the brasserie until 21.30.

venray.desc: After a day in Roermond, the centre of Venray makes a quiet change closer to the hotel, about 4 kilometres away. On the Grote Markt stands St Peter in Chains Church, also known as the cathedral of the Peel, with a tower of almost 80 metres. Around the square you can have a coffee or lunch on a terrace.
venray.credit: Photos: Dosseman, giggel, WoodenSpoon and Sindala via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA and CC BY), cropped.

maasduinen.desc: If you want some peace after a day among the shops, drive to De Maasduinen: the longest belt of river dunes in the Netherlands, with over 4,500 hectares of woodland, heath, drift sand and fens between the Maas and the German border. At the visitor centre in Well you will find walking and cycling routes.
maasduinen.credit: Photos: Lieblingsgouda, Steven Lek, Carelbullens and Jonathation via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA), cropped.

arcen.desc: In Arcen, the Kasteeltuinen Arcen (Arcen Castle Gardens) bring together more than fifteen gardens around a 17th-century castle, from a rose garden and an Oriental water garden to the tropical glasshouse Casa Verde. Hertog Jan brews its beer in the same village. Please note: the gardens are closed in winter.
arcen.credit: Photos: Vincent van Zeijst and Kasteeltuinen Arcen via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0), cropped.
